author: Roger Cleaveland
title: Sacred Heart men's basketball has six players with Connecticut ties. The connections run deep - NewsBreak
text:
By Roger Cleaveland ,
19 hours ago
Redshirt freshman guard Kevin Pikiell (21) talks with Sacred Heart men's basketball coach Anthony Latina during a practice. Latina and Pikiell's father, former UConn great Steve Pikiell, coached togetther at Central Connecticut as assistants under Howie Dickenman. Steve Pikiell is now the head coach at Rutgers (Courtesy of Sacred Heart Athletics)
FAIRFIELD — In addition to having a team that Sacred Heart men’s basketball coach Anthony Latina believes could compete for a Metro Conference title this season, the Pioneers have a roster that should pique the interest of Connecticut basketball fans and historians.
Sacred Heart (1-0) not only has six players with state ties on its roster this season, but the group includes some interesting connections and intriguing storylines to follow.
One guy is related to a beloved UConn player from Jim Calhoun’s first years in Storrs. The father of another current Pioneer was an All-American at Syracuse who played eight years in the NBA.
Yet another is part of one of the most storied families in Connecticut high school basketball history, and one more member of this year’s team had two brothers with him at Sacred Heart team last season.
What makes the Sacred Heart story even better is that Latina believes most or all those guys with Connecticut ties could have a big impact within the Pioneers program, if not this season, then before their careers are finished.
He expects 6-foot-3 junior guard Jojo Wallace, who played for New Milford High and South Kent, to be among the best offensive players for the Pioneers and possibly in the entire conference this season. Wallace at 21 points in Sacred Heart's season-opening win over Coast Guard on Monday.
Sacred Heart men's basketball 6-foot-3 junior guard Jojo Wallace, who played high school basketball at New Milford and South Kent, transferred to the Pioneers this season a transfer from Southern New Hampshire, where he was second nationally in scoring at 24.8 points per game. Wallace is the son of former Syracuse All-American and New York Knicks' first-round draft pick John Wallace. (Sacred Heart Athletics )
Wallace is the son of former Syracuse star John Wallace, who led the Orange to the national championship game his senior year and was a first-round draft pick of the New York Knicks.
“Jojo Wallace was at Southern New Hampshire last year, where he finished second in the country in scoring (at the Division II level) at 25 points per game,” Latina said. “He is just a scoring machine.”
Another outstanding offensive player expected to make a big impact is Glastonbury’s Samson Reilly, a high school star at East Catholic where he played for his father Luke Reilly Sr. and became a GametimeCT All-State player while leading East Catholic to two state championships.
Reilly played one season at Quinnipiac before transferring to Sacred Heart.
“He had a storied high school career and also did a lot of good things for Quinnipiac,” Latina said. “He is an elite, elite, elite shooter that can change the game at any given time. He is a guy who can make three threes in a minute and really change the complexion of the game.”
Junior guard Samson Reilly is expected to play a significant role for the Sacred Heart men's basketball team. Reilly from Glastonbury, played at East Catholic High under his father Luke, who was a high school teammate and co-captain with Pioneers coach Anthony Latina in 1991. (Sacred Heart Athletics)
His brother Luke Jr. is currently playing college basketball at Florida Southern, and his cousin Joey was a former player at Sacred Heart.
Overall, the family of the 6-foot-2 junior shooting guard is among the most prominent and successful ever in Connecticut. Reilly’s grandfather Joe and great uncle Gene were very successful high school coaches. His uncle Joe is the Wesleyan men’s basketball head coach.
Latina play for Joe Reilly Sr. at South Catholic and was high school teammates of Luke Sr. and Joe Jr.
Junior guard Samson Reilly is expected to play a significant role for the Sacred Heart men's basketball team. Reilly from Glastonbury, played at East Catholic High under his father Luke, who was a high school teammate and co-captain with Pioneers coach Anthony Latina in 1991. (Sacred Heart Athletics)
Another player on this year’s Sacred Heart team with a rich tradition of basketball is 6-3 redshirt freshman guard Kevin Pikiell, the son of former UConn standout point guard and Bristol native Steve Pikiell . Steve, who played for the Huskies from 1986-91, was a two-time captain at UConn who went into coaching is now the head men’s basketball coach at Rutgers University.
Mooda Gittens is also a redshirt freshman guard for the Pioneers this season. His brother Dashon Gittens led Sacred Heart in steals (49) last season was second on the team in assists (89) and third in scoring (13.5 ppg).
Although Dashon graduated, their older brother Donte has been with the Sacred Heart program since 2022, first as director of basketball operations and the last two seasons as an assistant coach. Their mother is a very well-respected program director within the Hartford Boys & Girls Club.
Sacred Heart men's basketball assistant coach Dante Gittens has had two brothers play for the Pioneers while he was on staff. Dashon played last season while Mooda redshirted and is expected to play this season. (Sacred Heart Athletics)
Latina said he has very close ties with the Gittens, Pikiell and Reilly families, so he knew he was getting high-character people with elite work ethics, high basketball IQ's and overall just a great understanding of what it takes to build teams and programs.
“Obviously in terms of the Gittens family, his brother is on my coaching staff so I know them well,” Latina said. “Steve Pikiell, Kevin’s father, he and I worked together for three years at Central Connecticut, so we are very good friends from our days working on Howie Dickenman’s coaching staff.
“Then obviously my connection with the Reillys goes back to my high school days. Sam’s father and I were captains together at South Catholic High School in 1991, and we have been friends for a long time. So, I have known Sam forever.”
He said he believes all three will thrive at Sacred Heart, especially since he has brought in so many experienced transfers around them.
Sacred Heart men's basketball redshirt freshman Mooda Gittens is the third member of the Gittens family to play for the Pioneers. (Sacred Heart Athletics)
“Sam is probably a little more ready to make an impact right now, but every time I talk to Kevin or Mooda, I remind them, ‘I don’t ever want you to settle. Your time is going to come,’” Latina said. “I would be shocked if all three aren’t very, very good impact players for us sometime before their careers are over.
“We are thrilled to have all three. We think they make us a lot better not only on the court but off the court, because they improve the overall culture of our program.”
